# Git Panel
## How To Build
A GitPanel should be built as a reusable component that will be reused throughout the rest of the codebase.  A component is configurable through arguments or properties that alter its behaviour, appearance, and details.  A GitPanel should encapsulate all of its own reusable behaviour, while leaving 
## Theme
Drawn in the [Theme](../../theme/index.md#theme): its surfaces, text, lines, accent, and status colours are the theme's roles, named as the theme names them, in both dark and light mode, never colours of its own.
## Title
null
## Counted
false
## Height
fit
## Scrolls
true
## Scrollbar
always
## Panel
It has no header: its contents start at its top edge, on the theme's base surface.
It shows no count of what it lists.
It is only as tall as its contents need, taking no more of its sidebar's height.
Its contents scroll on their own when they are taller than it, with a permanent scrollbar along its right, as the Scrollbar says.
## Pitch
A very basic git panel for the repository the ProjectDirectory is in, as the [Git](../../../scope/git/index.md#git) knows it: see what has changed at a glance, write a commit message, commit, push, and pull.
## Description
A compact panel. It is shown only while the project is inside a git repository.
## Look

content.text:
The git panel now fills the whole height of its sidebar view instead of being only as tall as its contents. `piton check` reports no problems and `piton build` wrote 84 files.

- **Panel height:** changed from "fit" to "fill", so it runs from beneath the ribbon to the window's bottom.
- **Layout:** the branch and summary stay at the top, and the message box, Generate and Commit stay along the bottom.
- **Few or no notes:** the gap between top and bottom is simply left empty in the panel's background colour.

**Anchors the code should follow:** `GitPanel` `#panel`, `#look` and `#scrolling`, and `LeftSidebar` `#views`.
